solutions.blurb: Saving moons, saving planets: the Moon keeps Earth's 23.5-degree tilt in check, which keeps our seasons and climate stable (NASA).

solutions.title: MOSAiC Expedition: A Year Frozen in the Arctic Ice
solutions.blurb: MOSAiC was the first year-round expedition into the central Arctic to study its climate system (MOSAiC).

solutions.title: Mote Marine Laboratory
solutions.blurb: Mote scientists have restored more than 216,000 corals to Florida's Coral Reef, and their restored corals now spawn (Mote figure).

solutions.title: Mountain Gorilla Recovery
solutions.blurb: Rangers, vets and communities in Uganda, Rwanda and the DR Congo pulled mountain gorillas up from Critically Endangered (IUCN).

solutions.title: Mr. Trash Wheel Family
solutions.blurb: Baltimore's Trash Wheels intercept about 500 tons of trash a year before it reaches the harbor and the Chesapeake Bay (organization figure).

solutions.title: Namami Gange (India)
solutions.blurb: India's Namami Gange programme has created or rehabilitated 4,263 million litres a day of sewage treatment for the River Ganga (government figures).

solutions.title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's Roman telescope launched Aug 30, 2026 to L2: Hubble-sharp images 100x wider, a census of planetary systems, first images by early 2027.

solutions.title: NEO Surveyor
solutions.blurb: NASA NEO Surveyor is the first space telescope built to find hazardous asteroids, including dark ones hidden in the Sun's glare.

solutions.title: NEOSSat Asteroid and Debris Telescope (Canada)
solutions.blurb: Canada's NEOSSat circles Earth every 100 minutes, scanning near the Sun for asteroids and comets and tracking satellites and debris (CSA).

solutions.title: Nepal Doubles Its Tigers
solutions.blurb: With rangers, wildlife corridors and over 450 community anti-poaching units, Nepal nearly tripled its wild tigers in 13 years (NTNC).

solutions.title: NEWater, Singapore's Recycled Water (PUB)
solutions.blurb: NEWater is high-grade reclaimed water from PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency, made from treated used water in a three-step purification process at 4…

solutions.title: NISAR (NASA–ISRO)
solutions.blurb: NISAR, a NASA and ISRO radar satellite launched from India on July 30, 2025, scans nearly all of Earth's land and ice twice every 12 days, even through clouds.

solutions.title: The Ocean Cleanup
solutions.blurb: The Ocean Cleanup removes legacy plastic from ocean garbage patches and intercepts it in rivers: more than 65 million kilograms caught as of October 2026.

solutions.title: Ocean Voyages Institute
solutions.blurb: A sailing nonprofit that has pulled more than 850,000 pounds of plastic from the Pacific Gyre in 10 voyages (nonprofit figure).

solutions.title: Oceanites: Antarctic Penguin Census
solutions.blurb: For more than 30 years, Oceanites has tracked penguin populations on the rapidly warming Antarctic Peninsula and shares the data openly (Oceanites).

solutions.title: OCO-2 Orbiting Carbon Observatory (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's OCO-2 satellite has measured carbon dioxide around the planet since 2014, showing where carbon is released and where forests and oceans absorb it.

solutions.title: Okavango Delta: The River That Ends in a Desert
solutions.blurb: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is a near-pristine inland delta whose waters drain into the Kalahari sands instead of the sea (UNESCO).

solutions.title: One Tree Planted
solutions.blurb: Since 2014, One Tree Planted has planted more than 171 million trees with 489 partners in 84 countries (organization figure).

solutions.title: OpenET Satellite Water Data
solutions.blurb: Free satellite data on how much water crops and land use, now for all 48 contiguous states, with more than 13,000 registered users.

solutions.title: Orbital Data Centers
solutions.blurb: Data centers in orbit run SI chips on solar power and radiate waste heat into space, with no water-cooling towers.

solutions.title: OSIRIS-APEX and Apophis 2029 (NASA)
solutions.blurb: On April 13, 2029, asteroid Apophis passes about 20,000 miles from Earth.

solutions.title: PACE (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's PACE reads the color of the ocean to track phytoplankton, the base of the marine food web, plus aerosols and clouds.

solutions.title: Palau National Marine Sanctuary
solutions.blurb: The Palau National Marine Sanctuary makes about 80% of Palau's exclusive economic zone a no-take area, with the other 20% kept as a Domestic Fishing Zone.

solutions.title: PAME: Protecting the Arctic Marine Environment
solutions.blurb: PAME is the Arctic Council working group for the protection and sustainable use of the Arctic marine environment (PAME).

solutions.title: Pan-STARRS Near-Earth Object Search
solutions.blurb: Two telescopes on Haleakalā, Maui, that in 2021 found nearly as many near-Earth objects as the rest of the world's observatories combined.

solutions.title: Papahānaumokuākea National Marine Sanctuary
solutions.blurb: Designated in 2025 as America's 18th national marine sanctuary, Papahānaumokuākea covers 582,570 square miles of Pacific Ocean around Hawaiʻi (NOAA).

solutions.title: Parker Solar Probe (NASA)
solutions.blurb: The first spacecraft to fly through the Sun's outer atmosphere, helping scientists understand the space weather that affects life and technology on Earth.

solutions.title: Penguin Watch: Count Penguins from Home
solutions.blurb: On Penguin Watch, anyone online counts penguin adults, chicks and eggs in camera photos to help scientists understand their lives and environment.

solutions.title: Penobscot River Restoration (Maine)
solutions.blurb: After two dams came out of Maine's Penobscot River, nearly 5.93 million river herring climbed the Milford fish lift in 2025, up from about 590,000 in 2015.

solutions.title: Permafrost Pathways
solutions.blurb: Permafrost Pathways connects science, people and policy to address Arctic permafrost thaw and support affected communities (Permafrost Pathways).

solutions.title: Phytoplankton, the Ocean's Oxygen Engine
solutions.blurb: Tiny ocean plants produce about half of Earth's oxygen, making phytoplankton one of the planet's most important natural systems.

solutions.title: Plant-for-the-Planet
solutions.blurb: Started by a 9-year-old in 2007, Plant-for-the-Planet trains young Climate Justice Ambassadors and restores forests, including Mexico's Mayan forests.

solutions.title: Plastic Bank
solutions.blurb: Plastic Bank pays collectors in vulnerable communities to gather ocean-bound plastic, exchanged at local branches for income, food vouchers and school supplies.

solutions.title: Plastic Odyssey
solutions.blurb: Plastic Odyssey sets up small recycling factories in places with no recycling system, turning plastic waste into useful products and local jobs.

solutions.title: Plato (ESA)
solutions.blurb: ESA's Plato will use 26 cameras to hunt for Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars, with launch planned for March 2027 on Ariane 6.

solutions.title: Polar Bears International
solutions.blurb: Polar Bears International works through research, policy and on-the-ground conservation to protect polar bears and their sea-ice habitat.

solutions.title: Posidonia Seagrass Meadows
solutions.blurb: The Mediterranean seagrass Posidonia oceanica forms meadows that are thousands of years old and store carbon in the seafloor (CEAB-CSIC).

solutions.title: Predator Free 2050 (New Zealand)
solutions.blurb: Predator Free 2050 is a nationwide goal to eradicate rats, possums, feral cats and mustelids from Aotearoa New Zealand, led by the Department of Conservation.

solutions.title: PREFIRE Polar CubeSats (NASA)
solutions.blurb: Two shoebox-size NASA satellites measure the far-infrared heat that Earth's poles send into space (NASA JPL).

solutions.title: Project Seagrass
solutions.blurb: Project Seagrass, a UK charity, has planted more than 150,000 seagrass seeds to bring back underwater meadows (organization figures).

solutions.title: PROMICE and GC-Net: Greenland Ice-Sheet Weather Stations
solutions.blurb: PROMICE and GC-Net put automatic weather stations on the Greenland ice sheet and share the data openly (PROMICE).

solutions.title: Psyche (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's Psyche used a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 to head for a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029, to learn what a planet's core is like.

solutions.title: PUNCH (NASA)
solutions.blurb: Four suitcase-sized NASA satellites image the Sun's corona and solar wind together, in 3D, since March 2025.

solutions.title: Rainforest Connection
solutions.blurb: Solar-powered Guardian listening devices and SI detect chainsaws in real time; Rainforest Connection reports more than 726,000 hectares of rainforest…

solutions.title: Ramses (ESA / JAXA)
solutions.blurb: ESA and JAXA's Ramses must launch by spring 2028 to meet Apophis before its 2029 Earth pass.

solutions.title: RADARSAT Constellation Mission (Canada)
solutions.blurb: Three Canadian radar satellites watch Canada's land, coasts and Arctic day and night, through cloud and smoke, with about 250,000 images a year.

solutions.title: Redonda Island Restoration
solutions.blurb: Redonda went from a dusty moonscape to a wildlife haven and is now one of the largest protected areas in the Caribbean (Fauna & Flora).

solutions.title: Restoring the Lake Depths Foundation
solutions.blurb: A Nevada nonprofit whose ROVs and volunteer divers pull submerged trash from Lake Tahoe, from the surface down to 1,640 feet: over 13 tons in summer 2024 alone.

solutions.title: Rewilding Europe

solutions.title: River Cleanup
solutions.blurb: River Cleanup and its volunteers have recovered more than 4.39 million kg of waste from rivers worldwide and aim for 1,000 plastic-free rivers by 2050.

solutions.title: Room for the River (Netherlands)

solutions.title: Ross Sea Region Marine Protected Area

solutions.title: Route of Parks of Patagonia (Chile)

solutions.title: Saharan Dust Feeds the Amazon
solutions.blurb: Every year about 27.7 million tons of Saharan dust falls on the Amazon, delivering some 22,000 tons of phosphorus that the rainforest needs (NASA).

solutions.title: Salt Marshes
solutions.blurb: Salt marshes are nurseries for more than 75% of fisheries species and buffer shorelines from erosion and floods (NOAA).

solutions.title: Sargassum Watch System (USF)
solutions.blurb: The University of South Florida uses NASA satellite data to track the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt and warn coasts about seaweed blooms (USF).

solutions.title: SARSAT Search and Rescue Satellites (NOAA)
solutions.blurb: NOAA's SARSAT satellites relay distress beacon signals to rescuers; the international system has supported more than 50,000 rescues worldwide since 1982.

solutions.title: SCAR: Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research
solutions.blurb: SCAR initiates, develops and coordinates international scientific research in the Antarctic region, including the Southern Ocean (SCAR).

solutions.title: SCISAT Ozone Watch (Canadian Space Agency)
solutions.blurb: Canada's 150 kg SCISAT has measured the chemistry of the ozone layer since 2003, with a special focus on Canada and the Arctic (CSA).

solutions.title: Sea Turtle Conservancy
solutions.blurb: Sea Turtle Conservancy works in 8 countries, has tagged and monitored more than 550 turtles and trained over 1,200 researchers (nonprofit figures).

solutions.title: Seabin

solutions.title: Seagrass Meadows

solutions.title: SeaTrees

solutions.title: Copernicus Sentinel-2C (ESA)

solutions.title: Copernicus Sentinel-3 (ESA / EUMETSAT)

solutions.title: Copernicus Sentinel-5P (ESA)
solutions.blurb: Copernicus Sentinel-5P maps the gases in the air we breathe, covering the whole planet every day with its Tropomi instrument (ESA).

solutions.title: Copernicus Sentinel-6B (ESA / NASA)
solutions.blurb: Sentinel-6B, launched November 17, 2025, continues the precise record of global sea level that began in the early 1990s.

solutions.title: Seychelles Marine Spatial Plan and Debt-for-Nature Swap
solutions.blurb: Seychelles turned a debt-for-nature swap with The Nature Conservancy into a plan that protects 30% of its waters (State House Seychelles).

solutions.title: SMAP Soil Moisture Active Passive (NASA)
solutions.blurb: SMAP maps the water in Earth's soil from space, helping improve predictions of weather, floods and droughts (NASA).

solutions.title: SmartICE: Sea-Ice Safety for Northern Communities

solutions.title: SOCCOM: Robot Floats in the Southern Ocean
solutions.blurb: SOCCOM is a multi-institutional program focused on the Southern Ocean and its influence on climate, using floats and models (SOCCOM).

solutions.title: SOHO Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (ESA / NASA)
solutions.blurb: Watching the Sun nonstop since 1995, SOHO helps experts predict solar storms and has found more than 5,000 comets (NASA).

solutions.title: SOLAR-1 (NOAA)
solutions.blurb: NOAA's SOLAR-1 (formerly SWFO-L1) watches the Sun from L1, about one million miles from Earth, streaming space weather data to forecasters in real time.

solutions.title: Solar Orbiter (ESA / NASA)
solutions.blurb: ESA and NASA's Solar Orbiter took the first close-up images of the Sun's poles, coming within 42 million km of the Sun.

solutions.title: SOOS: Southern Ocean Observing System
solutions.blurb: SOOS facilitates and enhances global Southern Ocean observations by coordinating fieldwork and sharing data (SOOS).

solutions.title: South Georgia Habitat Restoration
solutions.blurb: Two charities raised £10 million to clear rats and mice from South Georgia, and on 8 May 2018 the island was declared rodent-free (SGHT).

solutions.title: Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics
solutions.blurb: Life extension in GEO: two MEVs have docked with three satellites, and the Mission Robotic Vehicle and three pods launched July 21, 2026 (company figures).

solutions.title: SPHEREx (NASA)

solutions.title: Starfish Space Otter
solutions.blurb: The first Otter launched October 1, 2026 for NASA's SSPICY mission, inspecting up to four dead satellites and rocket bodies from 2027.

solutions.title: Sungai Watch
solutions.blurb: Sungai Watch stops plastic in Indonesian rivers with trash barriers, daily collection and sorting, plus upcycling, working in Bali and Java since 2020.

solutions.title: Surfrider Foundation
solutions.blurb: Surfrider Foundation volunteers protect the ocean, waves and beaches, and in 2025 they removed 338,383 pounds of trash from U.S.

solutions.title: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
solutions.blurb: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault stores backup copies of the world's crop seeds free of charge, more than 100 metres inside an Arctic mountain (Seed Vault).

solutions.title: SWOT (NASA–CNES)
solutions.blurb: SWOT measures more than 95% of Earth's lakes larger than 15 acres and rivers wider than 330 feet, the first global survey of fresh water.

solutions.title: Tallurutiup Imanga National Marine Conservation Area
solutions.blurb: Tallurutiup Imanga, in Nunavut, protects Arctic waters where narwhals live alongside thousands of seabirds, next to Inuit communities (Parks Canada).

solutions.title: Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper / Planet)
solutions.blurb: Tanager-1, built by Planet with a NASA JPL-designed spectrometer for the nonprofit Carbon Mapper, pinpoints methane and CO2 plumes from single sources.

solutions.title: TEMPO Air Quality Mission (NASA)
solutions.blurb: From geostationary orbit, NASA's TEMPO measures air pollution over North America every daylight hour, a first from space (NASA).

solutions.title: Terraformation
solutions.blurb: Terraformation grows native, biodiverse forests from seed to canopy across the tropics and Hawaii, funding seed collection, nurseries, planting and monitoring.

solutions.title: The SeaCleaners
solutions.blurb: Mobula cleanup boats catch plastic close to where it starts, and in Malaysia one boat turned 135,000 pieces of debris into community walkways.

solutions.title: Three Invisible Shields
solutions.blurb: Three natural shields protect Earth: the heliosphere, the magnetosphere, and the atmosphere with its ozone layer, deflecting solar wind and most harmful UV-B.

solutions.title: Three Trees for Every One Removed
solutions.blurb: Saving Planets' own forest rule: plant three trees for every one removed, so each removal becomes a net gain for habitat, soil and shade, and is easy to verify.

solutions.title: International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration
solutions.blurb: About 100 scientists from the UK, US, South Korea, Germany and Sweden are working out how fast Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier could raise sea levels (ITGC).

solutions.title: Titan
solutions.blurb: Titan is a prebiotic time capsule, and NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft explores it from 2034, building radar, power and autonomy tools that matter for Earth.

solutions.title: Tonle Sap: The Lake That Reverses a River
solutions.blurb: Tonle Sap, the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia, is a UNESCO biosphere reserve whose flooded forests shelter villages and fish (UNESCO).

solutions.title: TRACERS (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's twin TRACERS satellites fly through Earth's polar cusps to study magnetic reconnection, a key driver of space weather.

solutions.title: Trees for Life: Restoring the Caledonian Forest
solutions.blurb: Trees for Life is rewilding the Scottish Highlands, bringing back the Caledonian forest, of which less than 2% survives (Trees for Life).

solutions.title: Trees for the Future
solutions.blurb: Partnering with East African farmers on regenerative farms: 450M+ trees grown and 99,000 acres restored (nonprofit figures).

solutions.title: Trout Unlimited
solutions.blurb: Trout Unlimited restores and reconnects cold, clean rivers, reconnecting 1,052 miles of streams in its 2024-25 season (Trout Unlimited).

solutions.title: The Science of Tsunami Detection
solutions.blurb: Deep-ocean buoys, satellites, GPS signals and seafloor cables spot tsunamis in the open ocean so coastal communities get time to reach high ground.

solutions.title: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
solutions.blurb: Tubbataha, a no-take marine park of 96,828 hectares in the Philippines, protects pristine coral atolls and the sea life that seeds the Sulu Sea (UNESCO).

solutions.title: Methane Alert and Response System (UNEP)
solutions.blurb: The UN's satellite methane alert system has sent more than 3,500 alerts about major leaks in 33 countries, and responses rose from 1% to 12% in a year.

solutions.title: U.S. Deorbit Vehicle (NASA / SpaceX)
solutions.blurb: NASA selected SpaceX to build the U.S.

solutions.title: Veggie Space Garden (NASA)
solutions.blurb: NASA's Veggie garden grows fresh food on the International Space Station; in 2015 astronauts ate the first lettuce grown in it (NASA).

solutions.title: Vigil (ESA)
solutions.blurb: ESA's Vigil will watch the Sun from L5, giving up to four to five days' notice of certain space weather effects.

solutions.title: Voyager 1 and 2 (NASA)
solutions.blurb: Launched in 1977, the twin Voyagers are in interstellar space, and on Nov.

solutions.title: Waterkeeper Alliance
solutions.blurb: Waterkeeper Alliance unites hundreds of local Waterkeeper groups that patrol and protect more than 6 million square miles of rivers, lakes and coastlines.

solutions.title: Webb and 2024 YR4
solutions.blurb: How the James Webb Space Telescope tracked asteroid 2024 YR4 in February 2026 and ruled out a 2032 Moon impact, two years before ground telescopes could.

solutions.title: WeForest
solutions.blurb: WeForest has grown more than 118 million trees and has 100,000 hectares of forest under restoration and conservation (WeForest).

solutions.title: Whales, Ocean Gardeners
solutions.blurb: Whale waste carries nutrients to the ocean surface and fertilizes phytoplankton, the tiny plants at the base of the ocean food web (NOAA Fisheries).

solutions.title: WWF Arctic Programme
solutions.blurb: Since 1992, WWF's Global Arctic Programme has worked for a well-managed, biodiverse and resilient Arctic (WWF Arctic).

solutions.title: Yellowstone Wolves
solutions.blurb: Gray wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995 after nearly 70 years; in January 2026 at least 84 lived in the park, in eight packs (NPS).

solutions.title: Zero Debris Charter (ESA)
solutions.blurb: The Zero Debris Charter sets shared targets to stop creating space debris by 2030; by May 2026 it had 228 signatories from 34 countries (ESA).
